title: How do you plan an anniversary dinner at home in Dubai?
body_html:
An anniversary dinner at home works best when three decisions are settled early: the menu's tone, who serves, and the timing of the evening. Everything else — flowers, table setting, the toast — falls into place around them. For a dinner hosted for family or friends, our event catering team in Dubai can build the menu and service around the date; a private chef booking covers the same question for a smaller table.

Settle the tone before the menu

  • Recreate or explore: a menu built around dishes the couple already loves, or a new menu chosen for the occasion. Both work; mixing both in one evening rarely does.
  • Shared plates or plated courses: shared plates suit a relaxed table where conversation runs; plated courses suit a formal toast between courses.
  • One personal dish: a dish from the wedding, a first trip or a family recipe gives the menu its story without a speech.

Service style options

StyleSuitsWatch out for
Chef cooking and servingCouples and small tables of up to sixKitchen access and finish time
Plated courses with a serverLarger tables where hosts want to sit downCourse timings agreed in advance
Delivered courses, hosts serveIntimate evenings at homeHeating and plating instructions

Timing the evening

A simple outline keeps an anniversary relaxed: guests or the couple arrive to drinks; the first course lands about thirty minutes later; the main follows once plates are cleared; dessert and the toast close the evening. Agree when the chef finishes cooking and whether dessert service is included, so the last part of the night is not improvised.

Details that make the evening personal

  • A table setting in the couple's colours rather than a default.
  • Dietary needs of both partners confirmed, including anything a doctor or dietitian has advised.
  • Gifts and cards handed over after service, not across the dinner table.
  • A short toast scheduled between the main and dessert.

What to confirm before the evening

  • Date, guest count and whether it is a couple or a family table.
  • Menu tone: recreated favourites or a new menu.
  • Service format and who serves each course.
  • Arrival, first-course and dessert times.
  • Kitchen access, and where the team works and leaves.

A worked outline (hypothetical)

A couple hosts ten guests for a golden anniversary. The menu is built around three dishes from their wedding year, served plated with one server, with the first course at 19:45 and dessert at 21:15. Gifts are presented after dessert service, and the chef leaves the kitchen clear by 22:00. The outline is hypothetical; it shows the decisions sequencing rather than a recorded booking.

To plan the menu and service for an anniversary at home, send the date, guest count and your menu direction through our events page. The dinner party timeline guide covers the full evening hour by hour.
